- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, reduce forecasted price targets; model tends to overreact to negative sentiment.  
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 1.0) and price is rising, cap forecast peaks to avoid overshoot; model often overestimates upward momentum.  
- If recent price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), model tends to overpredict further decline — adjust downward bias.  
- Forecasting horizon 30d: model consistently overestimates early in the period (first 5–10 days) and underestimates late (last 10–15 days) — apply downward bias toward end of horizon.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent spike (e.g., +1.09 or higher) followed by a drop, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast after spike, especially if sentiment turns negative.  
- When sentiment is neutral or volatile (±0.5), model tends to overfit recent trends — use smoothing or lagged average to reduce noise.  
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% in first 5 days, apply a 3–5 day decay factor to reduce forecast magnitude.  
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after a spike, model often fails to anticipate — reduce forecast by 10–20% for 2–3 days post-spike.
